profile.reading: This facility is attributed in the registry to DataBank. DataBank Ltd. was established in 2005 in a historic former Federal Reserve Bank building in downtown Dallas, Texas, that had been converted to a data center in 1999, per DataBank own corporate history page fetched this session. DataBank was acquired in July 2016 by a group of investors led by DigitalBridge, per that same page. DataBank own history page also lists a series of acquisitions expanding its footprint, three Salt Lake City area data centers from C7 Data Centers plus facilities in Cleveland and Pittsburgh from 365 Data Centers in January 2017, Lightbound, an Indianapolis based provider, in December 2018, United States and United Kingdom data center assets from zColo in December 2020, and four Houston area data centers from CyrusOne for 670 million dollars in January 2022. A trade press article fetched this session, from pe-insights.com, reports that DigitalBridge agreed to sell a 27 percent fully diluted equity stake in DataBank to Swiss Life Asset Management and EDF Invest for about 1.2 billion dollars, expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2022, reducing DigitalBridge own stake to about 15.5 percent and yielding DigitalBridge about 230 million dollars in cash proceeds. DataBank own history page states the company now operates more than 65 data centers across more than 27 markets. The operator own dedicated page for this facility, Plano, designated DFW3, fetched this session, confirms the address already on file, 8375 Dominion Pkwy, Plano, TX 75024, and states 12 MW of critical IT load and 72,230 IT square feet.

reading.body:
DataBank Plano Data Center in Plano, Texas, publishes 12 MW of IT capacity across 72,230 square feet of technical space, operated by DataBank.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 1200 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 300 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

DataBank Plano Data Center holds 1 published certification: FedRAMP (authorization to host US federal government workloads). Together these qualify the facility for regulated workloads spanning security auditing, payments, and healthcare data, though which specific tenants rely on which certification is not disclosed.

Texas has 23 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 15 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 399.41 MW. DataBank Plano Data Center contributes 12 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
